facts.text: New Orleans barbecue shrimp is never barbecued: the style was born at Pascal's Manale, Uptown, in 1954 by the family's account, head on shrimp in a pan sauce of butter, black pepper, Worcestershire, garlic and lemon.

Stuffing is cooked inside the bird and dressing in its own dish, by the usual distinction, though the two share ingredients and many use the words interchangeably; in the South dressing is the common word however it is cooked, and Southern dressing is often made with cornbread.
